title: Safepath rollout heuristic notebook
content:
Quick brain-dump of heuristic ideas and a lightweight checklist for the next small-batch rollout (personal scratchpad). Goal: increase confidence in fast canary flips for model flips and quantization probes without heavy manual coordination.

High-level idea: score each micro-cohort by a small safety vector and let traffic controller gradually nudge cohorts according to score. Score = weighted sum(latency_stability, error_rate_delta, quality_delta, client_affinity). Default weights conservative, tuned per release.

Safety vector components (observable/measurement):
- latency_stability: rolling-p95 delta over baseline (30m window) normalized to 0..1
- error_rate_delta: 5xx + model-assert-fails / total requests (30m)
- quality_delta: small synthetic prompt set (fast eval harness) fail rate OR auto-metric (bleu-ish for routings). fallback to human-spot-check if ambiguous.
- client_affinity: how sticky is the client to previous model (token-cohort stickiness). low stickiness -> smaller risk when flipping.

Example safety thresholds (conservative starting point):
- p95 latency change <= +40ms
- p99 latency change <= +120ms
- error_rate_delta <= +0.25% absolute
- quality_delta <= -0.8% relative (on smoke prompts)
If any single threshold breached for 3 consecutive 5m buckets -> auto-pin that cohort and remove from gradual ramp for 30m, notify oncall.

Traffic shaping primitives to use:
- leaky-bucket per-cohort token reservoir (smoothing ramp and preventing burst overrun)
- soft-weights for multi-route traffic (able to divert to fallback model or lower-capacity variant)
- warmup priming (preload KV caches by replaying recent prefixes for seeds in cohort)
- sticky routing TTL (short, e.g., 60s) during initial ramp to avoid state explosion

Warmup recipe (cheap):
1) identify top 200 prefixes for cohort (last 24h sampling)
2) generate warmed KV requests at 10% of cohort rate for 3 minutes prior to traffic shift
3) monitor cache hit rate and tail latency; if hit-rate < 40% after warmup, delay ramp +5 minutes and retry one more warmup iteration

Pin strategy notes:
- allow manual pin for enterprise tenants (>= dedicated) that opt out of auto-rollout. Use tenant metadata to bypass scoring.
- for host-api free-tier cohorts, default to aggressive decays (fast revert) to preserve global SLOs.

Quick checklist before flip (single operator flow):
- [ ] confirm release has passed stale evals and smoke tests (CI artifacts attached)
- [ ] run local quick-audit (script: tools/release/audit_quick.sh <build>) -> ensure model variant id matches release note
- [ ] pick 3 warmup cohorts (low, med, high traffic) and run warmup recipe
- [ ] open ephemeral dashboard tab: rollout/curation/<release-id> (p95/p99/error/quality)
- [ ] initial cohort weight = 0.5% for 5m, then 1% for 10m, then multiply by 2x increments until target or threshold breach
- [ ] set auto-pin rules live in controller and arm slack alerts (channel: #release-watch)

Rollback / quick-escape rules (ops-safe):
- immediate rollback if error_rate_delta > +1% for any cohort during ramp
- immediate rollback if user-visible hallucination/failure (customer complaint + confirm)
- soft rollback (halve weight) if latency_p99 > baseline +200ms but error rate stable

Experiment ideas to record:
- weighted scoring variant: penalize quality_delta heavier during US hours, latency heavier during EU night (regional SLOs differ)
- probe progressive quantization where only non-critical layers quantized then progressively quantize bottom layers across waves
- model-fallback cascade: primary->lighter-quantized->small-LLM fallback for expensive tails (test cost delta vs user impact)

Telemetry to instrument (minimal):
- per-cohort: p50/p95/p99 latency, qps, 5xx, model-assert, cache-hit-rate, avg-kv-size, avg-sequence-length
- per-release: small synthetic prompt-set pass rate (5m), human check link counters, rollback count

Open TODOs (personal):
- tune weights for scoring function (which dimension should dominate?) -> run sim with historical traces (sandbox: infra/sim/rollout-sim-2025)
- build a tiny web UI to preview cohort scores before flip (mock: prototype in /tmp/safepath-ui)
- add integration test that simulates warmup failure (cache priming didn't take) and ensure controller delays ramp as expected

Notes-to-self:
- keep ramp steps small for tenants with high session-affinity (video/chat)
- document exact warmup RPC sequence for KV prefill (ops often forget TTL semantics)
- check prod quota rules: warmup blasts can trigger rate-limits for shared infer nodes, use tagging to bypass when necessary

Slack snippets to reuse for future flips:
- "Starting safepath canary for release <id> -> cohorts [low,mid,high], initial 0.5%"
- "Safety alert: cohort mid exceeded latency threshold at T+12m, pinning cohort and pausing ramp"

End-of-note: keep conservative by default. This is a personal scratchpad; turn into a proper runbook once a few flips succeed.

-- Mika
